One bird, and a status line that survives the next upgrade.

## What you get

**The status line keeps working after `brew upgrade`.** `canary settings
install` wrote the path Homebrew resolves to, which points inside
`Cellar/<version>/`. The next `brew cleanup` deletes that directory and the
bird vanishes from Claude Code with no error anyone sees. It now writes the
symlink, which is the half that survives. The shell hook was never affected:
`canary init` runs again on every shell start and healed itself.

If you installed with Homebrew before this release, run `canary settings
install` once more, or check the path in your `settings.json`.

**One bird per install, not two.** The bird that sang through the install
stayed on screen while a second one was drawn underneath it to sign off. Two
birds read as two installs. The singing bird's rows are now wiped when the last
step lands, the step log takes that space, and the bird that signs off is the
same bird, done singing.

**`--claude-only`.** canary is two birds from one binary, and the installer
wired both. Anyone who wanted only the Claude Code status line had to edit
their rc back by hand afterwards.

```sh
sh install.sh --claude-only
curl -fsSL .../install.sh | CANARY_CLAUDE_ONLY=1 sh
```

Homebrew never had this problem: it installs the binary and stops. `canary
settings install` on its own is still the shortest path to the Claude Code half.

**The installer stopped saying things that were not true.** It promised a
backup of `settings.json` even when there was no file to back up, and it
reported "added the hook" twice because the PATH line and the hook share one
function. It now names each of them, and only names a backup that exists.

## Also

The README opens with the gif, all three install paths are in the first screen
instead of four hundred lines down, and there is a second gif of the installer
itself. Both are recorded from tapes in the repo, so they can be re-rendered
rather than re-staged.

## Upgrading

```sh
brew upgrade canary
canary settings install   # rewrites the status line command, once
```
